notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/ambench__ambench --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored (deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wD-011) and unreviewed; reviewed_by stays null, no hardware backend exists and none was attached. The card's family-config GymnasiumDriver fits the upstream Gymnasium registration, so there is no deviation from the card. Both card entry symbols were confirmed by reading the clone: BaseEnv at source/ambench/ambench/tasks/base/base_env.py:29-30 and PressButton at source/ambench/ambench/tasks/press_button/press_button_env.py:17; native names PressButton and the package serves only PressButton-Am-EE-Abs-PID-Direct-v0, one of the registered PressButton task ids (source/ambench/ambench/tasks/press_button/__init__.py:11-16). The other registered task ids, the other robot/controller profiles (OmniHexa, FAHexa, UAHexa, UAQuad, L1, MPC, BaseJoint) and the other 11 task families are NOT COVERED. The package was not installed: README.md:42-43 requires a Linux host, a discrete NVIDIA GPU and Isaac Sim 5.1 with Python 3.11, and README.md:45-60 requires Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab before scripts/setup/install.sh builds acados and Pyroki; no network was used, nothing from the clone was imported or run, and the sim backend (gymnasium.make of the registered task) was not run. Because no upstream simulator could be started, the fake backend is the package's own pure Python kinematic stand-in for PressButton: it moves the end effector toward the commanded absolute pose, models the button press geometrically against the 0.004 success threshold and the 0.001..0.01 plunger travel, and returns the eleven observation members of the task at their real sizes (3/4/3/3/3/4/3/3/1/1/3; no array was truncated), the always-zero reward and the geometric button state. For the free end-effector profile the control body, base body and end-effector body are all ee_link (eef.py:63-65), so the fake's base_pos/base_quat/base_lin_vel repeat the end-effector values. The fake has no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, collisions, actuator or sensor model, so it is an F0 stand-in for the F1 Isaac Lab model and was never compared with Isaac Lab. The upstream _get_observations wraps the per-environment dict in {'policy': [...]} (press_button_env.py:99-106); the fake returns the dict directly, which the bridge publishes without the wrapper. The clone declares the action dimension (8, base_env_cfg.py:47) but not the Box bounds, which Isaac Lab builds outside the clone, so the fake publishes an unbounded eight-value Box; the runtime therefore has no per-element action bound and G8 awards CL2 with SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE. NOT COVERED: rendering (cap.world.render.v1 is not bound), snapshots/restore (the environment exposes no get_state/set_state), the wall-pose and button-scale event randomization beyond the button offset, and any comparison with a physical device. Expected family warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only arms the next reset), four G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space, reset and close (the DirectRLEnv base that provides them is outside the clone; the authoring guide allows the Gymnasium interface names as warnings), four G8.NO_UNIT for the simulator-derived integer inputs (seed twice, ticks) and the numeric action values, and G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE (no sourced action bound). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was emitted. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1/cap.world.reset.v1/cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. The gate digest above is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
